extracted.intended_audience: general readers, students and researchers interested in Anne Frank, Holocaust studies, publishing/editing of historical diaries
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria and standards used to judge, edit, authenticate, translate, publish, adapt, and teach a historically important personal diary (exemplified by The Diary of a Young Girl). Useful for editors, scholars, translators, teachers and curators handling similar archival diaries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forensic authentication of manuscript
rubrics_metrics.description: The material composition of the original notebooks and ink, and the handwriting found within them and the loose version were extensively examined; the handwriting attributed to Anne Frank was positively matched with contemporary samples of Anne Frank's handwriting, and the paper, ink, and glue found in the diaries and loose papers were consistent with materials available in Amsterdam during the period in which the diary was written.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use forensic methods (handwriting comparison, ink/paper/glue analysis, provenance checks) to determine authenticity; publish results of such studies. Note and explain anomalies (e.g., ballpoint-pen traces) and whether they are later additions or unrelated scraps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Version comparison and critical edition standards
rubrics_metrics.description: The 'Critical Edition' incorporated versions A and B, containing comparisons from all known versions, both edited and unedited, discussion asserting the diary's authentication, and additional historical information relating to the family and the diary itself.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Produce a critical edition by collating all surviving drafts/versions, annotate editorial interventions, provide provenance and authentication discussion, and present contextual historical notes. Clearly label which text corresponds to which version (A/B/revised drafts).

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial selection and redaction for publication
rubrics_metrics.description: Otto Frank made a representative but discreet selection from Anne's notebooks and loose pages, using the pseudonyms to protect the privacy of living and dead individuals; further entries were also deleted. Editors advised cuts (e.g., candid sexual content) when preparing the diary for early publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When preparing posthumous diaries for publication, editors commonly (a) select representative material, (b) remove or redact passages considered too intimate or potentially harmful to privacy, and (c) use pseudonyms to protect individuals. Document and justify deletions/redactions; where possible publish unexpurgated material later or in a critical edition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling of intimate/sexual material (censorship and age-appropriateness)
rubrics_metrics.description: Sections of Anne's diaries which had previously been edited out contained passages on pondering her sexuality, references to touching her friend's breasts, and her thoughts on menstruation; these later appeared in editions and triggered controversy, bans, and challenges on grounds of sexual content and 'homosexual themes.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess intimate content with attention to historical value vs. audience suitability. Expect community/school challenges when texts include explicit adolescent sexual content; prepare alternate classroom editions or contextual notes and be transparent about restored passages in critical editions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Physical provenance and material completeness
rubrics_metrics.description: Surviving manuscripts consist of three hardcover notebooks and up to 300 loose A5 sized pages, including pasted-in photographs, letters and other paper ephemera. Some volumes covering intervening periods are assumed lost.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record the physical state, format, and completeness of the manuscript (notebooks, loose pages, ephemera). Note missing periods/volumes and treat gaps in the record as part of provenance reporting; preserve and digitize original materials when possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency about editorial interventions and co-authorship claims
rubrics_metrics.description: The Anne Frank Fonds announced that the 1947 edition of the diary was co-authored by Otto Frank, arguing he created a new work by editing, merging, and trimming entries; other editors (e.g., Mirjam Pressler) later revised texts and added material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclose the extent of editorial rewriting, merging, or additions; be explicit about who edited/added material and how much was changed. Recognize that substantial editorial intervention raises questions of co-authorship and copyright, and document editorial methods to avoid misleading readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Translation fidelity and use of source texts
rubrics_metrics.description: New translations (for example Susan Massotty's 1995 translation) were based on the original texts and critical versions; the critical edition and later translations incorporated versions A and B.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Translate from most authoritative/original-source texts; indicate which draft/version formed the basis of a translation. Include translator notes explaining textual bases, choices, and any divergences from previous translations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Value as historical testimony and archival preservation
rubrics_metrics.description: Gerrit Bolkestein called for the preservation of 'ordinary documents – a diary, letters ... simple everyday material' to create an archive for posterity as testimony to the suffering of civilians during the Nazi occupation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize archival preservation of personal documents for their testimonial value. Provide context for readers about how ordinary personal writing contributes to historical understanding and collective memory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Literary and pedagogical assessment (style, insight, educational use)
rubrics_metrics.description: Critics described the diary as 'precocious in style and insight' that 'traces her emotional growth amid adversity' and it has been widely used in education and commemoration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating literary merit for teaching or adaptation, consider voice, insight, emotional development, and representativeness of lived experience. Balance literary appreciation with sensitivity to historical context and victims' dignity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adaptation authorization and fidelity to source
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain adaptations were authorized and in some cases allowed to quote literal passages from the diary (e.g., the 2014 play 'Anne' authorised and initiated by the Anne Frank Foundation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Obtain authorization from rights-holders for adaptations; decide and state how literal quotations will be handled. Consider ethical and legal permissions, and the balance between creative reworking and fidelity to the original text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publisher and market considerations affecting edits
rubrics_metrics.description: Publishers advised Otto Frank that Anne's candor about her emerging sexuality might offend certain conservative quarters and suggested cuts; early publication decisions reflected market and cultural sensitivities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect publishers to recommend edits based on perceived market and cultural sensibilities. Editors and executors should balance marketability with faithfulness, and document any cuts made for initial editions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responding to authenticity challenges and public controversy
rubrics_metrics.description: Holocaust deniers claimed the diary was fabricated, prompting forensic and legal investigations; courts and forensic studies supported authenticity. Controversies about missing pages, vandalism, bans, and ownership have arisen over time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be prepared to respond to authenticity and provenance challenges with documented forensic evidence, transparent editorial records, and legal clarification where necessary. Public controversies require clear communication about methods and evidence.
